by_judge.judge: HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR IS NOT HOLDING SITTING ON

narrative:
On August 27, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,626 cases across 51 benches and heard 989 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 37.7%. This represents a slight contraction compared to recent sessions, including 44.2% on August 25, 38.5% on August 20, and 42.0% on August 19. 

Benches exhibited varied disposal patterns across court halls. High disposal rates were recorded by Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar in Hall 20 (hearing 22 of 25 cases, or 88.0%) and Justice V. Srishananda in Hall 21 (hearing 65 of 94 cases, or 69.1%). Conversely, heavily loaded dockets saw moderate clearance: Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 19 heard 37 of 255 listed matters (14.5%), and Justice M. Nagaprasanna in Hall 14 took up 53 of 235 matters (22.6%) in one large list alongside 35 of 75 matters (46.7%) in another. Hall 22 did not hold sittings, leaving 34 scheduled cases unaddressed.

By procedural stage, Orders constituted the largest category with 961 scheduled cases and a 38.6% hearing rate (371 heard), lower than the 44.7% seen on August 25. Final Hearing matters lagged with 143 heard out of 597 scheduled (24.0%), closely mirroring historical conversion rates of 22.8% on August 19 and 29.4% on August 20. Admission stages saw 140 of 356 cases heard (39.3%), while Preliminary Hearings cleared 103 of 243 cases (42.4%).

Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the docket with 1,115 cases scheduled and 393 heard (35.2%), aligning with historical WP disposal rates ranging between 35% and 42%. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) achieved a 31.5% clearance rate (130 of 413 heard), down significantly from 54.1% on August 25 and 59.5% on August 19. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) reached 45.3% (140 of 309 heard), while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) saw a strong hearing rate of 60.6% (103 of 170 heard).
